# DESIGN.md — FACIALS BY VANESSA CT SKIN JOURNEY!

archetype: studio-personal
rationale: This is one esthetician's practice, written in her own first person. Her clients come back because of Vanessa herself: her patience, her honesty about not pushing products, and her rare expertise in melanin-rich skin. A personal studio direction lets her voice and her clients' words make the case, which no "spa" template could. The brand's own near-black and gold supply the dark, moody ground, so the dark-with-one-accent look comes from her tokens rather than being reached for.
interaction_level: L1

personality: [warm, assured, candid, glowing]

typography:
  display: "Roboto"
  body: "Roboto"
  scale: 1.333
  notes: |
    One face, used with conviction. The personality comes from contrast of weight and size, not from a second family.
    - Display headings: Roboto Light (300) at very large sizes, tracking tightened to -0.02em, stepping down 1.333 per level.
    - The single largest moment on the page is a client's words, not a heading.
    - Body: Roboto Regular, 18px, line-height 1.65, measure about 62ch.
    - Eyebrows: Roboto Medium, 12–13px, uppercase, letter-spaced 0.14em, gold on dark grounds. Keep small text small and rare.
    - Never use Bold for display. Heaviness would turn the voice corporate.
    - The business name is rendered exactly as "FACIALS BY VANESSA CT SKIN JOURNEY!". Set it once in the header at a modest size and let the headline do the speaking.

palette:
  primary: "#d9ae5f"
  secondary: "#0b0a09"
  accent: "#f4eee3"
  ground: "#13100c"
  surface: "#1f1a14"
  ink: "#ede4d3"
  muted: "#b3a58e"
  border: "#3a3127"
  application: |
    - **Ground and ink.** The page lives on the dark warm ground (#13100c), with ink (#ede4d3) for body text.
    - **Surface.** #1f1a14 is used only for the contact block and the open FAQ answer. Never use it for repeated tiles.
    - **Gold primary (#d9ae5f)** carries:
      - eyebrows
      - hairline rules
      - the phone number
      - the primary booking action, as a gold fill with #0b0a09 text (about 9.6:1)
    - **Cream accent (#f4eee3).** Used as a paper: a full-width band, at most twice on the homepage — under the pulled review and under the story. On those bands, text is secondary #0b0a09. Gold is never used as text on cream, because it fails contrast at about 1.8:1.
    - **Muted (#b3a58e).** Roughly 7:1 on both ground and surface. Use it for captions and review attributions.
    - **Why these neutrals belong to this brand.** The ground and surface are her own near-black warmed toward her gold, and the ink is her cream dimmed a step. The page reads as low candlelit warmth in Vanessa's colours, not stock charcoal.

composition:
  whitespace: generous
  photography: dominant
  card_usage: none
  mobile: |
    - Display type drops from about 4.5rem to about 2.6rem.
    - Gallery images go single-column at full width, with natural crops and no square-cropping of faces.
    - The phone number becomes a tap-to-call line.
    - A slim persistent bottom bar carries one action, "Call (860) 838-7039". It is mobile only, never shows on desktop, and sits clear of the accessibility widget's corner.
    - Booking form fields stack full-width, with 48px tap targets.

composition: |
  **Trust first.** Lead with Vanessa and with what her clients say she gave them that dermatologists did not: someone who understands dark skin, takes her time, and never pushes product. This is a destination for people who have been let down before. They need to trust the person before they browse treatments, so her voice and her clients' words come before any list.

  **Then the work, then contact.** Show the work in her own photographs at real scale. Name her treatments briefly and send the detail to the services page. End with an unhurried, direct way to reach her: the phone number and a booking request on this page.

  **No prices.** Price is not the argument here, and no prices appear anywhere. The only figures available come from the old site and are treated as out of date.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Make Vanessa's practice unmistakable in one screen.
      - **Headline:** the tagline "Healthy skin is a journey. Begin yours in Hartford.", set large in Roboto Light.
      - **Image:** the strongest gallery photograph. If one shows Vanessa at work or the treatment room, use it; otherwise use the most luminous skin close-up. That image is then not repeated in the gallery.
      - **Location:** one plain line, "200 Columbus Blvd 22nd Floor, Hartford, CT 06103, USA", exactly as written.
      - **Action:** a single gold button that scrolls to the booking request on this page. It never links to the old site's booking page.
      - No star count or review total.

  - id: story
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Let Vanessa introduce herself in first person, using the substance of her own About copy:
      - the serene room scented with essential oils
      - treatments tailored to the individual
      - eco-friendly products
      - a moment of peace as well as results
      Add, from her own writing:
      - that clients are "not a standard protocol"
      - her care with melanin-rich skin
      Rules:
      - Do not state a number of years. Her copy says both 9 and 10.
      - Never use "we", "our team", "therapists" or "reception". She works alone.

  - id: reviews
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Prove the specialism in clients' own words. This is the page's distinctive moment.
      - **The pulled quote:** pree dreams' line "After the first session with Vanessa my skin was GLOWING. My skin has NEVER glowed before." is set as the largest type on the site, on the cream band.
      - **The other four:** Tonya Noble, Tara Zayac, Viola Odenya and Judith Charlton-Lewis, in full as plain attributed text. They carry the case: expertise on Black skin, no product pushing, and a client travelling from NY monthly.
      Rules:
      - Use exactly these five reviews, verbatim, with their names. Nothing else.
      - No star graphics, no aggregate rating, no profile-photo grid.

  - id: offerings
    priority: essential
    show: "14 of 14 treatment names in 3 groups, names only, links to services.html"
    intent: |
      Tell a visitor what Vanessa does, using only the treatment names from her own site, in her three groups:
      - **Signature Facials & Targeted Treatments:**
        - Deep Pore Cleansing Facial
        - Anti-Acne Facial Treatment
        - Anti-Acne Back Treatment
        - Hydrofacial with Serum
        - Men Deluxe Facial
        - Teen Facial
      - **Clinical Peels & Skin Resurfacing:**
        - Chemical Peel
        - Brightening Pigment Peel
        - Microdermabrasion
        - Dermaplaning
      - **Virtual Skin Consultations & Routine Planning:**
        - Virtual Skin Journey Consultation
        - Virtual Skin Journey Follow-up
        - Teen Virtual Consultation (14–18 yrs old)
        - Complete Skin Journey Program
      Note that virtual consultations are available worldwide. Label the section "Services" or "Treatments", never "Menu".

      **On the homepage:** no prices, no durations, no deposits.

      **On services.html:** only five treatments get descriptive copy, drawn strictly from her own pages:
      - Anti-Acne Back Treatment
      - Virtual Skin Journey Consultation
      - Virtual Skin Journey Follow-up
      - Dermaplaning
      - Teen Virtual Consultation
      Every other treatment appears by name only within its group. Never write a description for a treatment her copy does not describe.

  - id: gallery
    priority: supporting
    show: "7 of 8, the hero image excluded"
    intent: |
      Let the remaining gallery photographs show the work and the atmosphere at a size that respects them.
      - Leave them uncaptioned rather than adding invented before/after claims.
      - Never use the logo or favicon images as gallery content.

  - id: faq
    priority: supporting
    show: "5 of 10, chosen for practical reassurance"
    intent: |
      Answer what a nervous first-timer actually asks, using only her own FAQ answers. Use these five:
      - How should I prepare? (arrive with a clean face; share concerns)
      - What should I expect during a facial?
      - What aftercare is recommended?
      - Is the spa accessible? (wheelchair accessible)
      - Is there parking? (valet parking)
      Reword lightly in her first-person voice. Add nothing.

  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      Make reaching Vanessa effortless and personal. Include:
      - (860) 838-7039, set prominently as a tap-to-call link
      - 200 Columbus Blvd 22nd Floor, Hartford, CT 06103, USA, exactly as written
      - "By appointment only"
      - **A booking-request form:**
        - Posts to Kora with form_type "reservation".
        - Collects name, email, optional phone, and a message about skin concerns and preferred times.
        - Follows the reCAPTCHA v2 lazy-load contract with the provided site key.
      Leave out entirely: email address, opening hours, social links, map embed.

avoid:
  - Any star rating, "Rated 5★ by 65 reviewers" or review count — not in the provided content
  - Prices, durations or deposits anywhere, including on services.html — the only figures come from the old site and are treated as out of date
  - Opening hours — the old site lists some, but they are not in the confirmed content; say "by appointment only" instead
  - Descriptions for treatments her own copy does not describe — Men Deluxe Facial, Teen Facial, Hydrofacial with Serum, Complete Skin Journey Program and the rest appear by name only
  - The old gmail address, or any email
  - '"We", "our team", "our therapists", "reception" — this is one woman writing in first person'
  - The old site's "LIMITED AVAILABILITY, CALENDAR IS FILLING UP" marquee, or any urgency language
  - Any "Pay over time / 0% APR" financing line
  - Stock spa clichés — orchids, stacked stones, bamboo, lotus icons, water-drop graphics
  - Tiles or cards for treatments, reviews or FAQs; treatments are named in type, never boxed in a grid
  - Gold text on the cream band, and gold gradients or metallic foil effects
  - Generic "luxury" filler like "indulge", "pamper yourself" or "ultimate in skincare luxury"
  - Links to skinjourneybyvanessa.com blog posts or its booking page, from the nav or anywhere on the site
  - Before/after labels or results claims on gallery images
  - Square-cropping faces or skin close-ups into uniform thumbnails
